structured_output.summary: Phase 6 (AI Gateway) meets its acceptance criteria with real, machine-checked evidence. All 194 owned Gateway methods are implemented across control, telemetry, runtime, multimodal and public-pricing surfaces; the ledger arithmetic reconciles exactly (gateway.json 61 + gateway-control.json 79 + gateway-runtime.json 54 = 194 against 196 frozen "ai-gateway" operations, with only connectRealtime and provision carrying machine-recorded Phase 7 ownership overrides and explicit reasons). Credential and plane isolation is enforced in code rather than asserted: engine.rs:475-498 binds OAuth/Runtime/Public authentication kinds, gateway/mod.rs:105-135 derives admin and IAM clients from one scoped OAuth identity and never copies it into the runtime or pricing planes, and routing.rs:20-54 allowlists only openai-beta and non-api-key x-portkey-* headers with case-insensitive duplicate rejection, sensitivity marking and byte/entry bounds. Streams are bounded and cancellable with distinct terminal policies, and EOF before the required terminal is a sanitized error (sse.rs:255-337); runtime replay is opt-in behind a separate permit type capped at five attempts and excluding 429 (routing.rs:64-91). Live status is precise: log-export start/cancel/download retain explicit experimental status and all live acceptance is deferred to Phase 8. Every attempt-1 finding is genuinely fixed, not papered over: the packaged 12-case bundle is now include_str!-bound and fully consumed with route/query/body/response assertions and unused-case rejection (gateway_contracts.rs:31, 565-653); the unverifiable Zod oracle comment is replaced by tools/verify-gateway-specimens.mts, which re-executes the frozen Zod schemas for 74 request/query/response parses, requires exact normalized equality, resolves the 12 independent cases' response schemas from the frozen fixture itself, and emits a reproducible artifact binding baseline, schema declarations, tooling inputs and the Rust test source by SHA256; tools/verify_native_fixtures.py:100-126 now parses Rust tokens (ignoring comments and quoted code) to require a literal test binding per bundle; examples/gateway.rs exists and actually compiles under the recorded --all-features runs; and the deleteResponse exemption is now a positive unit assertion. The recorded gate is honest: 36 commands in tools/check_phase.py commands_for(6) map one-to-one onto 36 check records, all exit_code 0, source_unchanged true, and source_sha256 equal to the SHA supplied for review. Spot-checked route and schema fidelity against the frozen baseline (configs.get, telemetry.filterBoundaries' deliberate organisationId deletion, the bespoke cache-hit-trend/user-trends slugs) is faithful, and docs/GATEWAY.md now distinguishes frozen-fixture evidence from hand-authored source-derived specimens instead of overclaiming. Two residual gaps keep this at 9 rather than 10: 19 of the 42 frozen independent gateway.json control cases are consumed by no test (and 11 more only for responses, not routes/queries/bodies), and nothing binds the declared response/request schema identities or routes to the frozen implementationSource that contracts/operations.json already records for all 194 methods. Both are evidence-strengthening opportunities, not unmet criteria or misstatements, so neither blocks advancement.

findings.description: The manifest-pinned independent corpus contracts/fixtures/typescript/test/openapi/fixtures/gateway.json contains 42 frozen cases for Phase-6-owned control methods, each carrying method, path, query/queryWire, body, responseBody and responseStatus. Only 23 are used: gateway_contracts.rs consumes 12 fully (log_exports 7 + rate_limits 5, with route/query/body/response assertions), and extension_reply() here consumes 11 for responseBody only (McpServers list/get/test/getCapabilities/getUserAccess/getConnections, UsageLimits list/get/listEntities, SecretReferences list/get). Nineteen cases are consumed by no test at all: AIGatewayGuardrailsClient (3, including syncMcpServers/getMcpServers), AIGatewayIntegrationsClient (1), AIGatewayMcpIntegrationsClient (1), six further AIGatewayMcpServersClient cases, four further AIGatewayUsageLimitsClient cases, three further AIGatewaySecretReferencesClient cases, and AIGatewayModelPricingClient (1). For those methods the route, query, body and response expectations are hand-authored source-derived literals even though independent frozen equivalents exist in the repository. The new gate command tools/verify_native_fixtures.py --require-test-bindings only proves that each bundle file is referenced by some test (verify_test_bindings at tools/verify_native_fixtures.py:100-126); it does not require that available frozen cases be exercised, so the corpus can stay 45% unused while the gate passes. docs/GATEWAY_CONTROL.md:71 describes this accurately ("remaining cases use manually authored source-derived fixtures"), so this is an unused-evidence gap rather than an overclaim.
findings.required_fix: Extend the control suite to consume the remaining 19 frozen gateway.json cases (and upgrade the 11 response-only uses to full method/path/queryWire/body/responseStatus comparisons, as gateway_contracts.rs:576-647 already does), resolving each case by call.className/call.member and failing if any case in the corpus is unconsumed; add that exhaustiveness assertion to the phase gate so an unused frozen control case fails the check rather than passing it.

findings.description: For the 12 independent cases the verifier takes responseSchema from the frozen fixture itself (line 98), which is authoritative. For the remaining 49 specimens in the GOLDEN table (crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_contracts.rs:1183 onward, e.g. "responseSchema": "GatewayConfigDetailSchema" at :1231) the schema name is hand-declared in the Rust test, and the verifier only proves that the specimen is accepted and exactly normalized by whichever schema was named. Nothing cross-checks that name against the frozen method's actual contract, and nothing checks the schema string passed to send_contract/send_model in the Rust source (for example "GatewayConfigDetailSchema" at crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/gateway/configs.rs:45) or the route literal against the frozen source. contracts/operations.json already records the complete frozen implementationSource per method, including the literal path expression and responseSchema identifier (see line 5548 for AIGatewayConfigsClient.get), so a declaring-schema-and-route binding is readily machine-checkable. As written, a permissive-but-wrong schema choice or a route typo in both the implementation and its hand-authored expectation would pass every recorded check for 182 of the 194 methods.
findings.required_fix: Add a check that, for every Phase 6 operation in contracts/native-operations.json, extracts the responseSchema/requestSchema identifiers and the path expression from the frozen implementationSource in contracts/operations.json and asserts they match both the schema strings used in the declared Rust source file and the schema names recorded in the GOLDEN specimen table; register it in tools/check_phase.py commands_for(6) so route and schema identity are machine-bound rather than reviewer-bound.

findings.description: "Independent fixtures pin exact bytes, headers, ordering and defaults for all five multipart forms" overstates independence. The five multipart operations cannot be expressed by the frozen JSON corpus at all: tools/schema-oracle.mts records exactly these five schemas under requiresNativeInput (docs/checks/phase-06.json:253, listing GatewayInferenceInputCreateImageEdit/ImageVariation/Transcription/Translation/CreateFileRequestSchema), and the frozen runtime fixture holds 49 of the 54 methods. The multipart expectations are hand-authored inside the test, which reconstructs the expected envelope from a Part list (crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_runtime_contracts.rs:423-452) with request builders at :455-522. The preceding sentence correctly says the frozen TypeScript fixture is consumed for the 49 JSON/text/binary cases, which makes the following "Independent fixtures" read as frozen-derived when it is not.
findings.required_fix: Reword docs/GATEWAY_RUNTIME.md:58 to state that the five multipart forms are pinned by hand-authored in-test byte expectations because the frozen corpus cannot express native file inputs (citing the schema-oracle requiresNativeInput record), reserving "independent frozen fixture" for the 49 cases that genuinely come from contracts/fixtures/typescript.

findings.description: All 79 entries in this new fragment use dotted namespace values such as "airs.gateway.admin_guardrails", while the other two Phase 6 fragments use Rust paths ("namespace": "airs::gateway::..." for all 61 entries in gateway.json and all 54 in gateway-runtime.json). tools/native_operations.py:118 emits rustMethods as f"{namespace}::{method}", so this fragment produces non-Rust identifiers like "airs.gateway.api_keys::create" in contracts/native-operations.json. The dotted style is pre-existing in management.json (56) and model-security.json (49), so this is a carried-forward inconsistency rather than a new defect, but Phase 6 adds the largest single block of it and the generated rustMethods field is the ledger's machine-readable pointer to public Rust API paths.
findings.required_fix: Normalize the namespace values in contracts/native-operation-mappings/gateway-control.json (and, for consistency, management.json and model-security.json) to Rust `::` paths naming the owning public type, and regenerate contracts/native-operations.json so every rustMethods entry is a resolvable Rust path.

findings.description: Metadata::new first rejects extension maps whose keys collide with a known field, then unconditionally rejects any non-empty extension map three lines later ("All five multipart schemas are strict, including future extension keys"). The first branch is therefore unreachable in effect, so the collision-specific check is dead code that reads as if the two cases were distinguished. Behavior is correct and the strictness is tested (every_native_file_shape_rejects_invalid_fields_collisions_and_bounds_before_dispatch at crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_runtime_contracts.rs:667), but the redundancy invites a future edit that relaxes the general rejection while assuming the first check still guards collisions.
findings.required_fix: Drop the redundant known-key branch at runtime_audio.rs:39-41 and keep the single non-empty rejection with its existing comment, or keep both and add a one-line note explaining that the collision check is retained deliberately for diagnostic specificity.
